subject.title: fix(heartbeat): warn when zero interval silently disables heartbeat

question: Should documented `heartbeat.every: "0m"` disables produce a warn-level diagnostic, an info/status diagnostic, or no diagnostic while likely accidental zero values such as `0s` warn?
rationale: The docs make `0m` the supported disable sentinel, so the diagnostic level and scope for existing zero-duration configs is an operator-experience and compatibility choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Warn only on likely mistakes
options.body: Keep `0m` as the canonical quiet or info-level disable path and warn on non-canonical zero values such as `0s`, `0h`, `0d`, or `00ms`.

options.title: Warn on every zero value
options.body: Accept warn-level output for existing `0m` disable configs and document that explicit heartbeat disables are now confirmed in logs.

options.title: Do not add zero diagnostics
options.body: Keep current disabled behavior unchanged and rely on docs or status surfaces instead of runtime warnings.

recommendation.title: Warn only on likely mistakes
recommendation.body: Keep `0m` as the canonical quiet or info-level disable path and warn on non-canonical zero values such as `0s`, `0h`, `0d`, or `00ms`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on disabled heartbeat guidance and related scheduler behavior.
